newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar strengthens on positive fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar strengthens on positive fundamentals.

text.p: The Canadian dollar strengthened on positive fundamentals to C$1.3681 (US$0.7310) from Tuesday morning's open of C$1.3693 ($US0.7303), bouncing off a 200-day moving average, dealers said.
The market has been bullish about the Canadian dollar since the Bank of Canada lowered interest rates last Thursday, said dealers.
And market players were optimistic about Canadian current account figures expected out this Friday.
"There are a lot of little positives out there," said Michael Gregory at Lehman Brothers.
"Chances are this Friday... we'll actually have our first current account surplus reported in 11 years," said Gregory.
A report on Canada's second quarter GDP is also expected Friday.
The 200-day moving average provided further support for the unit, dealers said. Trading was moderately heavy, showing signs of pent-up demand.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar was up to 1.0799 marks from 1.0783 marks, but sank to 78.62 yen from 78.77 yen.
